answer: Each applicant claims one tundra transect, locks a 70-credit bond to its key, and files a sheet counting juniper shrubs. The first costs 27 credits; the kth costs 27 plus 6 times k minus 1, so the 1000th costs 6021 and 1000 fakes cost 3,024,000 plus 70,000 locked. An auditor re-walks and recounts shrubs between its marble markers; a sheet outside tolerance, a reused key, or two transects per surveyor burns the bond. A rented-transect ring fails: copied sheets show identical counts at different coordinates. An honest surveyor pays 27 once and recovers the bond after a clean recount.
